overview.description: Clabber is a trick-taking card game of the Jass/Belote family, uniquely popular in Evansville, Indiana and surrounding areas. It is played with a 24-card deck (Ac-9) and features complex trump rankings and a 'meld' system where card combinations like 'Dad' (3-card sequence) and 'Mule' (4 Jacks) score bonus points. The game is highly strategic, requiring players to choose trumps carefully and compete for the prestigious 'last trick' bonus. It is colloquially known as 'Dad' after its most common sequence meld.
overview.deck: 24 cards (A, K, Q, J, 10, 9 of each suit)

history.origins: Brought to Indiana by German and Central European immigrants, Clabber is a local evolution of the European Klabberjass. It became a cultural staple in Evansville, often played in taverns and social clubs.
timeline: 19th Century: European Klabberjass variants arrive in the American Midwest.
Early 20th Century: The game stabilizes into the 'Clabber' format in Evansville, Indiana.
Modern: Still actively played in local tournaments and social gatherings, featuring distinctive 'special' score sheets.
history.evolution: The game retains the 'Bela' (Bell) and 'Darda' (Dad) terminology from its Jass ancestry but has specialized local scoring rules and jargon like 'Mule' for four Jacks.
history.cultural: In Evansville, Clabber is more than a game; it's a regional identity. The scoring 'XX' (turkey tracks) and the specific local vernacular distinguish it from generic Jass variants.

setup.players: 4 players in fixed partnerships (North-South vs East-West).
setup.equipment: 24 cards and a 'Clabber' score sheet (typically with 4 columns for tracking team scores and addition-checks).
setup.dealing: Dealer deals all 24 cards one at a time clockwise; each player receives six cards. The last card (dealer's) is turned face up; its suit is the trump candidate for the first round of bidding.

rules.objective: Be the first team to reach 500 points by winning tricks with high-value cards and declaring melds.
rules.gameplay: Must follow suit. If void in the led suit, you MUST play a trump. If trumps are led, you MUST 'overtrump' (play a higher trump) if able. The last trick scores a 10-point bonus.
keyRules: No card can be used in more than one meld (except Bell cards).
Meld must be announced during the first trick and shown before the second.
Trump-maker must have at least one card of the named suit to 'play'.
Turkey Tracks: An 'XX' on the score sheet when a team is set.

strategy.basic: Prioritize winning the Jack and Nine of trumps (The 'Jass' and 'Manille' equivalents). Count the 24 cards carefully to identify when it is safe to lead point-heavy cards like Aces and Tens.
strategy.intermediate: Use your 'Dad' or 'Fifty' sequences to force opponents into a set. Manage your trumps to ensure you win the last trick (10 pts) and secure the win.
strategy.advanced: Defensive play: If you are the opponents, focus on 'hicking' the bidders by forcing them to use their high trumps on low-value tricks, then taking the point-heavy late cards.
tips: Announce your Bell (K-Q) when playing the second card to ensure the 20 points.
Don't lead a lone non-trump Ace if trumps haven't been cleared; it's a prime target for a ruff.
The 'Mule' (4 Jacks) is almost an automatic round win - protect those Jacks at all costs.

trumpConfig.trumpSuitRanking: Jack highest, then 9, A, 10, K, Q in trump; non-trump A, 10, K, Q, J, 9
trumpConfig.overtakingRule: When void in led suit must play a trump; when trump is led or a non-trump was trumped must beat the highest trump in the trick if able, else play a trump.

meldConfig.initialMeldRequirement: Announce before playing to first trick; show before second trick

edgeCases.text: Renege: play ends; opponents score 162 plus meld. If both teams renege, hand is redealt by same dealer.
No card may be used in more than one meld except Bell cards. Equal rank and length in non-trump as highest meld: neither team scores meld.
Bell is announced when the second of the two cards is played or shown; Bell can be scored with other melds (e.g. Dad 'n' Bell).

customActions.description: Dealer deals all 24 cards one at a time clockwise so that each player receives six cards.
customActions.constraints: Dealer only; performed at start of each deal.

customActions.description: The dealer's last card is turned face up; its suit is the trump candidate for the first round of bidding.
customActions.constraints: Dealer only; after dealing, before bidding.

customActions.description: Say 'I play' to accept the turned suit as trump (first round) or to name a different trump suit (second round). Your team undertakes to take more points than the opponents.
customActions.constraints: You must hold at least one card of the trump suit you are proposing. First round: accept face-up card's suit. Second round: name a suit different from the turned card.

customActions.description: Play the first card to the trick. Player to dealer's left leads to the first trick; thereafter the winner of the previous trick leads.
customActions.constraints: Legal when it is your turn to lead; any card from hand.

customActions.description: Play a card of the suit that was led. You must follow suit if you can.
customActions.constraints: When following suit you must play a card of the led suit if you have one; no obligation to beat the cards already in the trick.

customActions.description: When you have no card of the suit led, you must play a trump if you have one. Only if you have neither may you play a card of another non-trump suit.
customActions.constraints: Void in the led suit; must play a trump if able.

customActions.description: When a trump is led, or a non-trump was trumped, you must beat the highest trump so far in the trick if you can; if you cannot beat it you must still play a trump if you have one.
customActions.constraints: When void in led suit and playing a trump, or when following to a trump lead; must overtrump if able.

customActions.description: During the first trick, announce scoring combinations (Dad, Fifty, Running 100, four of a kind, Mule, Bell). The team with the highest-ranking meld scores all their melds; show melds before playing to the second trick.
customActions.constraints: Must announce just before playing a card to the first trick; no card may be used in more than one meld except Bell cards.

engine.handRankingSystem: Trick rank: in trumps J, 9, A, 10, K, Q; in non-trump A, 10, K, Q, J, 9. No poker hand comparison.
engine.rankingSystem: Trick and meld points; first to 500 wins.
engine.deckDescription: A 24-card stripped French deck: Ace, King, Queen, Jack, Ten, and Nine in each of the four suits (Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, Spades). Used for Clabber and related Jass-family games in which only the highest six ranks are used.
engine.suitDescription: Four French suits: Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, and Spades, each with six cards (A, K, Q, J, 10, 9). Standard suit order and iconography.
engine.rankDescription: Six ranks per suit. In trumps: Jack (20 pts), Nine (14), Ace (11), Ten (10), King (4), Queen (3). In non-trump: A, 10, K, Q, J, 9. For sequence melds: A-K-Q-J-10-9.
engine.dealPattern: Six cards each, one at a time clockwise; dealer's last card is turned face up as trump candidate.

synthesis.shortDescription: Evansville's favorite trick-taking game. Use a 24-card deck, declare 'Dads' and 'Mules' for points, and watch out for the 'Turkey Tracks' if your team gets hicked.

prompts.human: You're in Evansville, sitting across from your partner. You have the 9 and J of trumpsâ€”the two most powerful cards. But you don't have enough sequences to win the meld. Should you play for the last trick or try to 'hick' the opponents on the first few leads?
prompts.ai: Game: Clabber. Players: 4 partnership. Deck: 24 cards (9-Ace). Special trump rank: J(20), 9(14), A, 10, K, Q. Melds: Dad (20), Fifty (50), Mule (200), Bell (20). Last trick: 10 pts. Rule: Must overtrump if void.

scoring.description: Cumulative score to 500. Points come from card values in tricks (J=20, 9=14 in trumps), melds, and the last trick bonus.
scoring.winCondition: The first team to reach or exceed 500 points wins.
scoring.splitRules: If the trump-making side fails to score more than the opponents (including melds), all their points for that round are forfeited.
